correctness.rationale: One-to-one reduction between rooted order-five de Bruijn cycles and 2-choice pairings at 16 graph vertices, accepted iff one 32-edge orbit. Independent Eulerian DFS generates precisely the same 2048 canonical cycles; two different dynamic programs agree on every one of 65536 circular cuts, and complete CSV, exact counts, moments and symmetry-orbit arithmetic are checked. The recurrence has standard induction proof, not mere experiment.

originality.rationale: Inspected public literature covers general palindromic subsequence algorithms, circular word unrestricted minima and cyclic LCS variants, while accessible own prior results count distinct scattered palindromic subsequences in three-one-run words or longest contiguous palindromic factors in de Bruijn cycles; none implies the entire new de Bruijn-restricted cyclic LPS spectrum. Actual indexed research searches under aliases failed to identify a dominating census. This is best-knowledge originality, not a global uniqueness certificate; inaccessible source full text and unindexed tables remain residual risks.
residual_risks: An earlier independent de Bruijn-specific numeric LPS census may be unpublished or unindexed.
Brodal et al. and Nicolas/Rivals source full articles were not inspected in entirety; the checked abstracts support limited rather than categorical comparison.
Database semantic ranking is not a proof of absence, and available historical snapshots may omit additional findings.

value.rationale: Circular deletion-to-palindrome optimization is an established nonlocal string invariant (OEIS A318916). Exhaustive classification of the complete 2048-member order-five de Bruijn family determines sharp admissible values, their multiplicities, statistical moments and symmetry orbits; in particular it isolates a strict one-step gap from the unrestricted tabulated minimum 24. Prior contiguous-factor statistics do not supply these results. Finite natural complete census has intrinsic comparison value without speculative generalization.
